note: Defects this layer has actually shipped, or plausible neighbours of them,
written back into the code on purpose. tools/mutate-sql.sh applies each one
to a copy of the tree and requires some check to notice.
Every other tool here answers 'is the code right?'. This answers 'would we
know if it weren't?', which is a different question and the one that was
never asked. The slot invariant added after the code review was a no-op: it
was committed, trusted, and did not fire when the bug it existed for was put
back by hand. Nothing said so, because nothing tried.
`from` must occur exactly once. A pattern that matches nothing is a suite
error, never a pass -- a stale pattern would otherwise be scored by whatever
the checks say about unmutated code, which is this tool's own failure mode.

mutations.name: collation-dropped
mutations.was: M1. MariaDB's REGEXP and = follow the operand's collation, which is case-insensitive by default, so "A" $== "a" was TRUE on the server and FALSE in SEL.

mutations.name: find-args-swapped
mutations.was: The reordering template that made Fragment::bindings() walk the output rather than return the pool.

mutations.name: binary-operand-not-cast
mutations.was: Found by the fuzz lane. HEX(1) hexes the number and answers "1"; SEL's TO_HEX(1) is "31".

mutations.name: pad-truncates-again
mutations.was: Found by the oracle. LPAD('7777', 2, '0') is '77'; SEL's PADL returns "7777".

mutations.name: min-of-one-argument
mutations.was: Found by the oracle. LEAST and GREATEST are variadic but need two arguments; SEL's MIN takes one.

mutations.name: bindings-unwalked
mutations.was: Code review. Returning the pool ignores reordering templates and repeated slots.

mutations.name: number-becomes-a-placeholder
mutations.was: The params-mode defect the fuzz lane found: no coercion of a bound string reproduces a bare decimal literal.

mutations.name: union-instead-of-merge
mutations.was: Code review. PHP's + keeps the LEFT value, so field-name normalisation was discarded and every lookup failed.

mutations.name: concat-treated-as-comparison
mutations.was: Class F. The collation fix keyed on the variant name `text`, which `&` also uses.

mutations.name: define-upper-cases-everything
mutations.was: Code review. Skeleton names are camel-case, so upper-casing every key made runtime skel registration silently dead.

mutations.name: negative-literal-unparenthesised
mutations.was: MariaDB reads -- as double negation and gets the right answer by luck; PostgreSQL and SQLite read it as a comment.

mutations.name: relation-slots-collide
mutations.was: Item 6 absorbed: the three relation skeletons merge two slot maps that were disjoint by inspection and by nothing else.

mutations.name: arity-fallback-ignored
mutations.was: The `*` key added for MIN. Without it an unbounded arity resolves no template.

mutations.name: kinds-unify-loosely
mutations.was: Found by the fuzz lane. IF(TRUE, TRUE, "A-1") is "TRUE" in SEL and 1 on the server.

mutations.name: bool-compared-to-a-number
mutations.was: Found by the fuzz lane. CAST(0 AS CHAR) and CAST(FALSE AS CHAR) are both '0'.

mutations.name: bool-compared-to-a-number-in-a-list
mutations.was: The same guard on the IN path. inOperator and binary() lower different operators, and the mutation runner found only one of the two was pinned.

mutations.name: regex-dotall-dropped
mutations.was: M1. Dotall is permanently on in SEL and off by default in the server.

mutations.name: regex-flag-by-count
mutations.was: Code review. Choosing the case-insensitive template by argument count made RMATCH(p, s, "") match case-insensitively.

mutations.name: binary-literal-broken
mutations.was: The BIN branch of Emit::literal, which no closed expression can reach -- SEL has no BIN literal. Only the corpus's value bindings get there.

mutations.name: sqlite-numbers-unquoted
mutations.was: The decision the whole sqlite dialect turns on. Bare 2.50 is a REAL that prints as 2.5, so `2.50 $== 2.5` becomes TRUE where SEL says FALSE.

mutations.name: sqlite-comparison-stops-coercing
mutations.was: The consequence of quoting numbers: without the cast, two quoted numbers compare as text and 2.50 == 2.5 is FALSE where SEL says TRUE.

mutations.name: sqlite-integer-division
mutations.was: SQLite's / between integers is INTEGER division: 10 / 4 is 2 where SEL says 2.5. A different operation, not an imprecise one.

mutations.name: sqlite-right-of-zero
mutations.was: Found by the fuzz lane on sqlite's first run. substr(X, -0) is substr(X, 0), which behaves like substr(X, 1), so RIGHT("a", 0) answered "a".

mutations.name: arity-not-enforced
mutations.was: sql/MAP.md has documented `arity` as narrowing a dialect's accepted argument counts since M1. The generator validated the field and nothing enforced it, so a narrowed entry took the call anyway and dropped the arguments its template did not name.

mutations.name: bool-becomes-a-placeholder
mutations.was: Found by the fuzz lane on sqlite. 1 = '1' is 0 in SQLite -- INTEGER and TEXT are different storage classes -- so a BOOL bound as a string made TRUE XOR TRUE answer TRUE in params mode and FALSE inline.

mutations.name: family-leaves-diverge
mutations.was: mysql-family is defined as the spellings MariaDB and MySQL agree on, and both leaves override nothing. An override added to one and not the other breaks that silently -- the two dialects would emit different SQL for the same rule and each would pass its own cases.

mutations.name: regex-promoted-without-checking
mutations.was: RMATCH moved from the mariadb leaf to mysql-family once MySQL 8.4 was asked and agreed. Downgrading it to a refusal is the interesting direction: a refusal is a legitimate outcome, so the oracle abstains and the coverage gate stops counting the entry at all. Only a case asserting the emitted string notices.
mutations.to: "RMATCH": "downgraded to a refusal by the mutation runner",

mutations.name: pg-text-operands-uncast
mutations.was: PostgreSQL will not coerce: upper(integer) and reverse(numeric) are `function does not exist`. SEL numbers ARE text values, so a NUM fragment reaches a text function legitimately.

mutations.name: pg-integer-overload
mutations.was: Given an INTEGER argument PostgreSQL resolves sign() to its DOUBLE PRECISION overload, so an expression that looks exact quietly leaves exact-decimal territory. A precision loss, not a type error.

mutations.name: pg-collation-dropped
mutations.was: COLLATE "C" is what makes the ORDERING half of the byte family agree: 'a' < 'B' is TRUE under the default collation and FALSE under "C", and SEL compares bytes.

mutations.name: pg-binary-cast-naive
mutations.was: The inner CAST AS TEXT dropped. convert_to takes text, so a NUM operand -- SEL numbers are text values, and BLEN(1+1) is an ordinary thing to write -- has no matching function and the query dies. The original form of this mutation targeted the old double-cast template and went stale when that was fixed; the hazard it names is still real, one layer in.

mutations.name: bool-in-a-numeric-comparison
mutations.was: 0 != FALSE is E_NOT_NUM in SEL. MariaDB and SQLite coerce the boolean to 1 or 0 and answer anyway -- a wrong answer with no error attached -- and it took PostgreSQL's `cannot cast type boolean to numeric` to make the gap visible.

mutations.name: raw-binding-unchecked
mutations.was: (string) on an array yields "Array" plus a warning, and that string is then spliced into a correlated subquery as if it were a join condition.

mutations.name: constant-validation-removed
mutations.was: M5. The translator answered 'can this be pushed down' without asking 'is this a SEL expression'. LEFT("abc", -1) translated into all four dialects and they answered '', '', 'ab' and 'abc'. Killed by every `!` line in the corpus and by every case in 16-constants.sqlt.

mutations.name: constant-negation-not-constant
mutations.was: The constancy test walking `bin` but not `un`. Every out-of-range argument in the corpus is written `-1`, which is a NEG over a literal, so the check would have looked present and validated nothing that mattered.

mutations.name: constant-check-runs-before-dispatch
mutations.was: Validating on the way in rather than on the way out. Every refusal the translator already had -- ABORT, an unportable regex, a BOOL where a number belongs -- would be replaced by the vaguer 'SEL rejects this expression'.

mutations.name: sqlite-comparison-claims-exactness
mutations.was: M5. SQLite's CAST(text AS NUMERIC) is an INTEGER to 19 digits and a REAL at 20, so CAST('99999999999999999999' AS NUMERIC) = CAST('99999999999999999998' AS NUMERIC) is 1 where SEL says FALSE. Without the caveat the corpus's 20-digit comparison is a DIFFER.

mutations.name: mysql-family-multiply-claims-exactness
mutations.was: M5. DECIMAL caps the result scale of a product at 30 on MySQL and 38 on MariaDB, and SEL has no cap, so 0.00000000000000000000000000000001 * 2 is 2e-32 in SEL and zero on MySQL. The corpus carries one expression past each boundary, so stripping the caveat is a DIFFER on both leaves and not just the one that found it.

mutations.name: constant-check-outermost-only
mutations.was: Checking only the outermost constant node, which is what the first version did. SEL is lazy, so FALSE AND (1 / 0 > 0) is constant and answers FALSE without dividing -- the AND passes, the division is never looked at, and (1 / 0) goes into the SQL. The same division beside a column was refused. Killed by the const.lazy.* cases. Not by the corpus: a `!` line asserts SEL raises, and SEL does not raise here -- it is lazy and answers FALSE. An expression SEL accepts and the translator refuses can only be asserted as a case.

mutations.name: caveated-entry-answers-anything
mutations.was: A caveat does not narrow what an entry may answer; it suspends the oracle's verdict for it. ansi's LOWER already carries unicode-case, so every disagreement it produces is reported as inexact-by-declaration and passes -- and no .sqlt case names LOWER on any dialect. The entry can therefore return the wrong function's answer. This is Class A with the check switched off by a field that was added for an honest reason.

mutations.name: exactness-invented
mutations.was: The reverse of mysql-family-multiply-claims-exactness, and the direction almost nothing checks: isExact() is only ever used to EXCUSE a difference, so declaring a caveat an entry does not need leaves the string unchanged and an agreeing caveated entry still counted as agreeing. CAUGHT, by sqlite.strict.allows-text -- the one case in 273 that puts $== under strict. That is the whole of what stops it: see exactness-invented-where-nothing-is-strict, which is the same edit one entry over and survives.

mutations.name: entry-withdrawn-silently
mutations.was: Withdrawing a working entry, the way ansi already withdraws the ones it cannot spell. A refusal is an outcome the oracle counts and never fails on, and the coverage gate measures Map::entry() LOOKUPS, which a withdrawn entry still performs -- while Map::entries() stops counting it as supported, so the denominator shrinks to match. Twenty of mariadb's sixty-seven supported entries have no .sqlt case at all, and every one of them can be turned off like this.
mutations.to: "ABS": "withdrawn: ABS of a DECIMAL widens the result type on some servers",

mutations.name: text-quote-escape-halved
mutations.was: The injection sql/cases/01-lexical.sqlt exists to stop, one dialect over. Every case in that file is --- dialect mariadb, so postgresql's and sqlite's quoting have no witness anywhere; and no expression in the corpus or in rows.json contains an apostrophe, so nothing ever asks either. lex.text.single-quote-doubles is the case that would have caught this, written for the wrong dialect.

mutations.name: family-leaf-diverges-where-no-case-looks
mutations.was: mysql.json's own notes say "adding an override to one leaf without the other fails the suite", citing MIRRORS in php/bin/sqlt. That holds only for entries some mariadb case reaches. No case reaches TRUNC, so this override makes MySQL emit a different string from MariaDB for it and the mirror never looks. Semantically identical, so the oracle agrees on both leaves -- which is the point: the family's claim is about BYTES.

mutations.name: placeholder-ordinal-counts-inlined-slots
mutations.was: The binding-order defect from M2, in the one form the suite cannot see. bindings() walks the output and skips inlined slots; join() must number placeholders the same way or the nth value lands in the wrong placeholder. Every shipped dialect spells its placeholder `?`, which carries no ordinal, so the error is invisible there -- and the one case that registers a numbered placeholder, pg.params.numbered-for-a-libpq-host, has no NUM or BOOL literal in front of its bound ones. Neither does the single --- mode debug case.

mutations.name: mirror-compares-mariadb-with-itself
mutations.was: A check on a check, which is what §7 of docs/SQL-TESTING.md is about, and the PHP array-union trap this layer has already shipped twice. `+` keeps the LEFT operand for a duplicated key, so swapping the operands makes the mirror re-run every mariadb case AS mariadb. The pass count is unchanged, the "also checked against a mirrored dialect" line still prints the same number, and the only thing that makes mysql.json safe to leave empty has stopped happening.

mutations.name: min-claims-exactness
mutations.was: Same shape as mysql-family-multiply-claims-exactness and, unlike it, unfalsifiable by the comparator. LEAST(17, 123.456) is 17.000 and SEL's MIN(17, 123.456) is 17, which is what numeric-scale declares -- but no corpus line mixes scales in MIN, and if one did, sqlo's compare() reads a NUM fragment through Dec::cmp, where 17.000 and 17 are one number. Only an expression that reads a computed number as TEXT can see this caveat doing anything.

mutations.name: exactness-invented-where-nothing-is-strict
mutations.was: exactness-invented, moved one entry over. That one was caught, by the single case in the suite that puts $== under strict -- sqlite.strict.allows-text. Six strict cases exist in 273, between them pinning the exactness of four entries; every other entry can be declared inexact for free. LEN is one, and after this the oracle can no longer fail on it.

mutations.name: value-binding-is-not-constant
mutations.was: The constant check not knowing about value bindings, which is how it shipped. §5.4 calls a value binding a constant inlined as a literal, so LEFT("abc", X) with X bound to -1 is as knowable as LEFT("abc", -1) and was as wrong. Killed by the mixed:edge-value-binding-is-constant corpus group.

mutations.name: assignment-value-not-validated
mutations.was: Stage 1 recording a definition without validating it. A definition nothing reads is dropped, so `A = 1 / 0; TRUE` translated to TRUE and every server answered TRUE where SEL raises. Killed by the const.assign.* cases.

mutations.name: eql-compares-bool-ness-only
mutations.was: The structural-comparison guard as it shipped: it asked whether both operands were BOOL, which let BIN through. TO_UTF8("a") EQL "a" is FALSE in SEL and answered 1 on MariaDB, MySQL and SQLite.

mutations.name: arithmetic-guard-forgets-bin
mutations.was: spec §4 says "BOOL and BIN are never numbers" and the guard implemented the first half. BLOB + 1 translated: MariaDB 2.0, MySQL 50, SQLite 1, PostgreSQL raises.

mutations.name: concat-accepts-a-bool
mutations.was: `&` left out of the kind guards because it is not arithmetic. FLAG & NAME concatenated, MariaDB answering '1a' and PostgreSQL 'truea', where SEL says E_NOT_TEXT.

mutations.name: function-arguments-are-unchecked
mutations.was: No argument-kind check for funcs existed at all. 26 functions accepted a BOOL and 26 accepted a BIN where SEL raises -- UPPER(BLOB) answered '1' on three servers and '\X31' on PostgreSQL.

mutations.name: byte-functions-lose-their-exemption
mutations.was: The other direction: over-refusing. BLEN, TO_HEX and the rest genuinely take bytes, and a guard that refuses them would make the BIN half of the layer unusable while every check still passed.

mutations.name: bare-binder-takes-the-scalar-field
mutations.was: The multi-field guard IN got at M4 and the bare binder did not. ANY(ITEMS, _ $== "AB-1000") is [] in SEL -- a row is a map and comparing a map against text is structurally false -- and was [1] on all four servers.

mutations.name: relation-row-gets-the-scalar-rule
mutations.was: source()'s scalar fallback swallowing a multi-field row: COUNT(I) folded to 0 where SEL says 3, HAS(I,"QTY") to FALSE where SEL says TRUE.

mutations.name: list-yielding-call-gets-the-scalar-rule
mutations.was: The same fallback reaching a call that yields a list, which bypassed the SPLIT/BTL/RGROUPS refusals under COUNT and HAS: COUNT(SPLIT("a,b", ",")) folded to 0 where SEL says 2.

mutations.name: has-over-a-relation-answers-from-fields
mutations.was: HAS folded by looking the key up in the binding's declared fields, which asks a different question from SEL's: HAS(ITEMS,"QTY") was TRUE where SEL says FALSE, HAS(SKUS,"1") was FALSE where SEL says TRUE.

mutations.name: relation-nests-inside-itself
mutations.was: A relation nested in itself reusing its own fixed alias, so the inner FROM shadows the outer: the predicate became `oi`.`qty` > `oi`.`qty` and all four servers answered [] where SEL answers with every order whose lines differ.

mutations.name: relation-binding-can-be-indexed
mutations.was: index() resolving a relation BINDING to a bare column reference. Outside an aggregate that is invalid SQL -- the alias is in no FROM clause. Inside one it emitted SQL byte-identical to the binder form and answered, where SEL raises E_NO_KEY.
mutations.from:
refuse('E_SQL_SHAPE',
                "{$obj['name']} is a relation, which is a list of rows; indexing it "

mutations.name: pg-binary-cast-parses-bytea-escapes
mutations.was: PostgreSQL's binaryCast as CAST(CAST({0} AS TEXT) AS BYTEA). text::bytea parses its input as a bytea literal, so any backslash changed the bytes or killed the query: BLEN('\\') was 1 against SEL's 2 and TO_HEX('a\\b') raised 22P02. A sweep of 13840 renderings gave 1290 server errors and 52 silent wrong answers, all on this dialect.

mutations.name: binary-cast-applied-to-a-bin-operand
mutations.was: binaryCast wrapping an operand that is already BIN. Harmless on the three dialects whose cast is idempotent and destructive on PostgreSQL, where the bytes go out through text and come back parsed as a bytea literal.

mutations.name: bin-is-parameterised
mutations.was: A BIN literal rendered as a placeholder rather than inline. The driver sends the bytes through the connection's text encoding: on PostgreSQL 130 of 256 single-byte values failed, 129 as invalid byte sequence and 0x00 silently. Inline was correct for all 256 on all four dialects.

mutations.name: two-bins-compared-as-characters
mutations.was: A byte comparison casting two BIN operands to CHAR. MariaDB and MySQL answer NULL when either side is not valid UTF-8, where SEL answers FALSE. The corpus's only BIN value was 7ac3a9 -- valid UTF-8, and precisely the byte string that could not show it.

mutations.name: in-relation-does-not-fold-null
mutations.was: skel.inRelation without the IS TRUE fold that `all` and `any` carry, which is how it shipped. A NULL among the subquery's rows makes x IN (...) answer NULL when nothing matches, NOT NULL is NULL, and the WHERE drops the row: NOT("flag" IN NOTES) selected one order where SEL selects three.

mutations.name: skeleton-caveat-is-ignored
mutations.was: skeleton() reading the template and never the caveat, which is how it shipped -- `skel` was the one section whose entries could declare an inexactness that never reached Fragment::caveats and that strict never refused. MariaDB's CASE pads the scale of a NUM branch and needs one.

mutations.name: mirror-exception-is-not-guarded
mutations.was: Not a defect this layer shipped: a defect the allow-list that hides defects could acquire. MIRROR_EXCEPTIONS names the one entry mariadb and mysql are allowed to disagree on, and an entry there silences the parity check for that name for good. Removing the entry must make parity fail -- if it does not, the exception was load-bearing for nothing and the check it guards has already gone vacuous.
mutations.from:
'skel.case' => 'MariaDB pads the scale of a CASE over NUM branches and '
        . 'declares numeric-scale for it; MySQL 8.4 does not. See mariadb.json.',

mutations.name: caveat-excuse-is-not-guarded
mutations.was: The same question asked of the other allow-list. coverage.json's caveats_unwitnessable excuses a declared caveat from ever being seen doing its job, which is the oracle being told twice not to look. Renaming mariadb's concat-null excuse must make the symmetry check name the caveat it can no longer account for. Needs a database: without one this is reported skipped, because the check that would catch it did not run.

mutations.name: key-regex-accepts-a-trailing-newline
mutations.was: How it shipped, in BOTH hosts, and the worst kind of defect this layer can have: they agreed, and they were both wrong, so no amount of comparing PHP against Python could see it. `^[0-9]+$` accepts "1\n" because PHP's `$` matches before a trailing newline without the D modifier -- and `(int)"01"` is 1 -- so V["01"] and V["1\n"] both resolved to element 1 where SEL answers E_NO_KEY. Dec::parse carries the D for exactly this reason and the SQL layer had not inherited it.

mutations.name: slot-regex-accepts-a-trailing-newline
mutations.was: The same slip in the template grammar. tools/gen-sql-map.mjs refused `{1\n}` because JS reads `$` strictly, and Map::define accepted it -- so the shipped map and a runtime-registered entry were being read by two different grammars, and only one of them was validated.
